# Tutorial: any clustering algorithm {#any}

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(selectiveHotelling)
```

The test needs only one thing from the clustering algorithm: a function `cl_fun` that takes
a data matrix and returns a vector of cluster labels. `selective_hotelling_bc()` reruns this
function on perturbed versions of the data and keeps the perturbations under which the
tested clusters are returned again.

The function must be **deterministic**: run twice on the same data, it must return the same
labels. Fix any random seed or random initialization inside the function, as below.

## Partitioning around medoids

```{r any-pam}
library(cluster)
set.seed(123)
X <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 2), matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 2) + 4,
           matrix(rnorm(100), ncol = 2) - 4)

cl_fun <- function(x) cluster::pam(x, k = 3, cluster.only = TRUE)
cl <- cl_fun(X)
table(cl)
selective_hotelling_bc(X, cl_fun, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, M = 1000)$pval
```

## A clustering function with a random step

If the algorithm uses random numbers, fix the seed inside the function and restore the
caller's random number stream afterwards:

```{r any-random}
cl_fun_random <- function(x) {
  old <- .Random.seed
  on.exit(assign(".Random.seed", old, envir = globalenv()))
  set.seed(1)
  kmeans(x, centers = 3, nstart = 5)$cluster
}
selective_hotelling_bc(X, cl_fun_random, k1 = 1, k2 = 2, M = 1000)$pval
```

The same approach works for community detection on a nearest-neighbor graph, as used for
single-cell data, or for any other method.

## What `selective_hotelling_bc()` returns

```{r any-return}
res <- selective_hotelling_bc(X, cl_fun, k1 = 1, k2 = 3, M = 1000)
c(pval = res$pval, T2 = res$T_obs, move_fraction = res$move_frac)
```

`move_fraction` is the fraction of steps at which the Monte Carlo path moved. Values far
below about $0.3$ suggest that the path barely explores the set of data sets that
reproduce the clusters, which lowers power but not validity (Chapter \@ref(details)).
